text:
sanjay: Brain dump from today's sync: we prototyped a lightweight "fastpath" sidecar to evaluate tenant residency/sovereignty checks at the POP. Key idea: accept read-only policy metadata (allowed_regions, deny_rules) signed by control-plane and cache per-tenant decisions for short window.

elaine: Quick question 3: does the sidecar authorize writes at all?

sanjay: Not by default. Writes are conservative and should be proxied to control-plane except when the tenant has an explicit "local-allowed" emergency flag. Reads (routing / hinting) can be served from cache.

josephine: Ops note: we measured cache hit rates ~82% for typical geo-routing traffic on canary POP. Average end-to-end p95 latency improved ~12ms for those requests. That said, cold-starts blow up control-plane qps, so warm-up is important.

mike: Implementation sketch: sidecar exposes a tiny unary gRPC Check API: Check(req) -> {allowed:boolean, version:string, source:"sidecar"|"cp"}. Cache entries keyed by (tenant, operation). Policy blobs signed with RSA-ECDSA v1 and include expiry. Sidecar verifies signature before applying.

elaine: Failure semantics: if sidecar cannot reach control-plane and no valid cached decision exists we need per-tenant policy: fail-open for "developer-tier", fail-closed for "regulated". That requires tenant metadata to include failure_mode.

josephine: Rollout approach: 1) only read-paths served initially, 2) use a 0.5% shadowing traffic flag to validate sidecar decisions against control-plane answers (no impact to client), 3) once stable, increase canary and enable small-scope write short-circuit for emergency-flagged tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary group pop-eu-1 deployed sidecar v0.2 -> 20 hosts, shadow traffic enabled, observed 3 mismatches in first 4h (investigating).

mike: Mismatches likely from timing drift on policy_version. Mitigation: include monotonically increasing policy_epoch in blobs and publish a policy_announcement SSE message before rolling patches. Sidecars should apply only when epoch matches or is greater; older blobs rejected.

elaine: Security: sidecars must authenticate to control-plane SSE. Propose SPIFFE mTLS with short-lived certs minted by control-plane CA; blobs are still signed so we have defense-in-depth.

josephine: Observability: trace span should contain fields: policy_version, decision_source, decision_cache_hit(bool), and policy_blob_id. Also emit a small audit event to central pipeline for each write decision (not for reads) that includes tenant, op, decision and policy_blob_id.

mike: Token-stamping idea: when control-plane issues client tokens we can optionally embed policy_version and tenant_failure_mode. Sidecar can trust stamped token to accept request without re-check until token expiry. Upside: fewer sidecar->control-plane calls; downside: revocation complexity.

elaine: We must be explicit about revocation: implement a short ack window for revoke events where control-plane issues a "revoke_bloom" push that sidecars consult before honoring stamped tokens. It keeps revocations eventual but bounded.

sanjay: Operator tooling + playbook: provide a forced-sync endpoint and a pop-quarantine operator action. Example operator curl: 
```bash
# force sync and quarantine pop
curl -X POST https://controlplane.int/admin/pops/pop-eu-1/quarantine \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" \
  -d '{"reason":"stale-policy-detection","policy_epoch":"2024-12-10-07"}'
```
Quarantine switches POP proxies to forward everything to regional gateways (no sidecar decisions).

josephine: Resource impact: current POC sidecar RSS ~55MB, cpu ~1% per core under baseline. We'll need to measure at scale for tiny POP hosts.

mike: Long-term: if we want stronger partition tolerance, evaluate a gossip-based region-list reconciliation (CRDT set) for allowed_regions only. Not for deny rules or revocations (hard).

elaine: Testing: add chaos tests that: - drop SSE for 5m and validate fail-mode, - corrupt a signed blob and assert rejection, - simulate clock skew and validate policy_epoch ordering.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pop-eu-1 -> after patching SSE retry logic, mismatch rate fell to 0 in last 2h.

sanjay: OK next steps I propose: 1) merge signed-blob verifier + policy_epoch handling, 2) add tracing fields + audit hook (writes), 3) roll out shadowing to two more POPs, 4) create operator runbook entry and schedule chaos validation.

mike: I'll send a proto PR and blob spec.

josephine: I'll handle canary expansion and telemetry dashboards.

elaine: Security will evaluate SPIFFE mTLS + revocation approach.

sanjay: Thanks all. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up that captures the operator surface, SSE contract, token stamping options, and the failure-mode matrix. Ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
